summary: Streaming partial-ack cascade causing duplicate tool/function invocations in serverless orchestration
summary_long: Customer reports duplicated downstream function executions when using the TS SDK's streaming client combined with a Step Functions style serverless orchestrator that replays sessions after client disconnects.
description:
Issue summary:
The customer (Nimbus Analytics) is seeing duplicated invocations of external tool endpoints (webhook-based function calls) when their orchestration retries a streaming session after an abrupt client disconnect. This is occurring for streaming responses with partial acknowledgements (per-message confirm) enabled in the TS SDK.

Impact:
- Duplicate side effects observed in production: duplicate billing events and duplicate downstream job runs.
- Affected ~3% of long-running orchestrations (~120/week) for this customer.
- Customer considers this a P1 due to data correctness and downstream cost impact.

Environment:
- Redwood prod region: us-east-1
- TS SDK version: 2.7.1 (customer-run), orchestration: AWS Step Functions invoking serverless workers via webhook endpoints behind CloudFront.
- Webhook consumer acknowledges function calls and performs idempotent checks, but duplicates still pass through due to varying confirmation tokens.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat session from TS SDK with per-message partialConfirm enabled.
2) During a long response (~>45s), simulate client network interruption (client process kill or ephemeral edge outage).
3) Orchestrator detects incomplete session, attempts replay/resume by creating a new client session and re-sends the same user prompt.
4) Streaming runtime delivers partial tool call confirmations; one instance shows confirmation token A, the resumed session presents token A' (token normalization/truncation) and the orchestrator re-sends the tool invocation to the webhook.
5) Consumer receives two distinct invocations and processes both (duplicates).
observed_behavior:
- Duplicate POST requests to customer's webhook within a 2-5s window for the same logical tool call.
- Confirmation tokens differ in length/encoding between original stream and resumed stream (example tokens in logs).
- Server-side logs show the Redwood streaming runtime generated two separate funcall records labeled with different stream session IDs.
expected_behavior:
- When a streaming session is resumed, the runtime should normalize idempotency/confirmation tokens so resumed requests are recognized as the same logical invocation and not re-delivered to webhooks.
- At most-once delivery semantics for tool/function calls within the bounds of the session's idempotency scope.
logs:
Excerpt from request log (timestamps truncated):
- 2026-03-08T16:22:03Z /stream A -> funcall webhook POST idempotency_token=eyJr...X (session s-123) -> 200 OK
- 2026-03-08T16:22:45Z client disconnect detected (session s-123)
- 2026-03-08T16:22:49Z orchestrator starts resume -> new session s-456
- 2026-03-08T16:22:50Z /stream A (resume) -> funcall webhook POST idempotency_token=eyJr...X~ (different encoding) -> 200 OK
Note: tokens differ by trailing modulus and a compressed header byte in the resume path.
investigation_notes:
- Slack thread: #support (link: slack.com/archives/C04SUPPORT/p167839) where Nimbus first reported duplicates.
- Dashboard check (console): per-route token counts show retry spike at 2026-03-08 16:22 UTC correlating to customer's reported window.
- Captured raw streaming frames from runtime show original funcall frame included 'confirm_token' field as base64url, while resumed stream replaced header with a hex-encoded prefix.
- Replayed requests through local staging with TS SDK 2.7.1 reproduced duplicate POST when using CloudFront+Lambda@Edge in front of webhook (header normalization by edge appears to mutate multi-part confirm header).
- No evidence this is a consumer-side mishandling; webhooks log distinct tokens.
hypothesis:
1) Edge/Proxy (CloudFront + Lambda@Edge) rewrites or splits idempotency/confirmation header during resume path leading to token normalization mismatch.
2) TS SDK generates a resume-compatible token but runtime path that handles resumed streams applies an alternate encoding (hex vs base64url) for confirm tokens.
3) Downstream idempotency checks fail because token canonicalization isn't consistent across original/resume paths.
mitigation_workaround:
- Customer temporary workaround: disable automatic resume/replay in the orchestrator (fail-open to the original session) and let client retry from scratch, or have webhook add a dedupe layer using a broader composite key (user_id + prompt_hash + approximate timestamp).
- Recommended short-term: enable strict canonicalization on customer edge (avoid header rewrites for confirm headers), or run webhook behind an ALB (avoids CloudFront Lambda@Edge rewrites).
actions_taken:
- Eng (ts-sdk) created a small reproducer and opened PR to add instrumentation around confirm token generation and normalization (see related PR).
- Ops added extended logging around confirm_token headers in prod route for Nimbus for the incident window.
- Support engaged Solutions Engineering to advise customer on temporary request dedupe pattern.
next_steps:
- Engineering to add deterministic canonicalization logic in streaming resume code path (TS SDK + runtime) to ensure confirm tokens use a single encoding across original/resume flows. Target: patch in 2.7.2.
- Ops to validate that edge proxies (CloudFront Lambda@Edge) are not normalizing headers; if they are, publish guidance for customers in the runbook.
- Customer to test the workaround removing Lambda@Edge manipulation and report results.
- Set follow-up check: verify no duplicates for 72 hours after patch/mitigation.
